title: How to Prepare Files and a Brief for a Translation Project
h1: How to prepare files and a brief for a translation project
description: Prepare translation projects for accurate, consistent results: editable files, target audience, glossary, style notes, context, review and a word count.
intro: Translation quality depends heavily on what the translator receives. Sending a scanned PDF with no context, no word list and no idea of the audience forces guesswork, and guesswork leads to inconsistent terms and extra rounds of corrections. With a little preparation, translators work faster, quote more accurately and deliver text that sounds right to your readers. This article explains what to prepare before you hire.

faq.q: How are translation projects usually priced?
faq.a: Often by word count of the source text, sometimes by hour or page for special formats.

faq.q: Why do translators want editable files?
faq.a: Editable files can be counted accurately and returned in the same layout.
A list of key terms with their approved translations, so they stay consistent.

faq.q: Should a second person review the translation?
faq.a: For important or public content, a review by another native speaker is wise.
For internal drafts it may be. For customer-facing text, have a human translate or edit it.
